///WEB REPORT/// A SMALL SHEEN WAS OBSERVED AFT OF CGC BERTHOLF BY CREW ON SATURDAY 25JAN14. SHEEN WAS CONTAINED INSIDE A BOOM AND WAS LIGHT, NO MORE THAN 1 METER LONG ACROSS THE STERN OF THE VESSEL, LIKELY CAUSED MINIMAL FLUID. SHIP'S FORCE TROUBLESHOT AND FOUND A SMALL LEAK (APPROX 1 DROP EVERY 30 SECONDS) FROM A HYDRAULIC ACTUATOR FOR A STERN DOOR. DRIP WAS IMMEDIATELY CONTAINED AND SHEEN DISSIPATED WITHIN 15 MINUTES. CUTTER WAS BOOMED THE ENTIRE TIME. CUTTER HAD DEPARTED DRYDOCK DAILY ROUND OF SHIP WOULD HAVE PREVENTED PROLONGED PERIOD OF LOST HYDRAULIC FLUID. BELIEVE EXTREMELY MINIMAL AMOUNT LOST.

CALCULATIONS ARE STILL BEING PERFORMED TO IDENTIFY HOW MUCH WAS POTENTIALLY RELEASED, BUT IT IS ESTIMATED TO BE BETWEEN 500 AND 1000 POUNDS OF XYLENE. SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 28.340278, -82.706389 (Explicit)
Report Description
7/19/18 (THURSDAY NIGHT): SWO AND OER WERE NOTIFIED BY A PRIVATE CITIZEN OF AN UNKNOWN SHEEN IN PASCO COUNTY. THE SHEEN WAS OBSERVED IN A FINGER CANAL IN HUDSON NEAR THE INCIDENT ADDRESS. THE CALLER BELIEVED THE SHEEN WAS COMING FROM A COMPANY INSTALLING A BOAT LIFT. THE CALLER REQUESTED A CALLBACK FROM DEP. OER SPOKE TO THE CALLER, WHO SAID THAT FD AND S.O. WERE ON-SCENE. OER SUGGESTED NOTIFYING USCG VIA NRC, ALSO. OER DID NOT RESPOND, DUE TO THE IMPENDING NIGHTFALL, AND SINCE OTHER RESPONDERS WERE ON-SCENE. OER DECIDED TO FOLLOW UP IN THE MORNING. 7/20/18: OER VISITED THE SITE, WHICH WAS BEHIND THE HOUSE AT 12608 FOURTH ISLE, WHERE QUALITY DOCKS WAS WORKING ON A BOAT DOCK. NOBODY WAS AT THE HOUSE OR WORK SITE AT THE TIME. OER SAW A SILVERY SHEEN AROUND THE COMPANY"S SMALL BARGE, AND AT THE NORTH END OF THE FINGER CANAL. THE REMAINING RAINBOW SHEEN HAD DISSIPATED NATURALLY. THE INITIAL CALLER SAID THAT THE SHEEN WAS FIRST NOTED ON 7/19 AROUND 3PM, AND WAS HEAVIER RAINBOW SHEEN AT THAT TIME. HE ADDED THAT THE FD WAS ON THE PHONE WITH USCG, BUT DID NOT KNOW IF USCG RESPONDED. 7/23/18: NO FURTHER CALLS RECEIVED. THE REMAINING SHEEN WAS ALLOWED TO DISSIPATE NATURALLY. A $50 FLAT-FEE NRDA IS APPLICABLE.

OER SUGGESTED NOTIFYING USCG VIA NRC, ALSO. OER DID NOT RESPOND, DUE TO THE IMPENDING NIGHTFALL, AND SINCE OTHER RESPONDERS WERE ON-SCENE. OER DECIDED TO FOLLOW UP IN THE MORNING. 7/20/18: OER VISITED THE SITE, WHICH WAS BEHIND THE HOUSE AT 12608 FOURTH ISLE, WHERE QUALITY DOCKS WAS WORKING ON A BOAT DOCK. NOBODY WAS AT THE HOUSE OR WORK SITE AT THE TIME. OER SAW A SILVERY SHEEN AROUND THE COMPANY"S SMALL BARGE, AND AT THE NORTH END OF THE FINGER CANAL. THE REMAINING RAINBOW SHEEN HAD DISSIPATED NATURALLY. THE INITIAL CALLER SAID THAT THE SHEEN WAS FIRST NOTED ON 7/19 AROUND 3PM, AND WAS HEAVIER RAINBOW SHEEN AT THAT TIME. HE ADDED THAT THE FD WAS ON THE PHONE WITH USCG, BUT DID NOT KNOW IF USCG RESPONDED. 7/23/18: NO FURTHER CALLS RECEIVED. THE REMAINING SHEEN WAS ALLOWED TO DISSIPATE NATURALLY. A $50 FLAT-FEE NRDA IS APPLICABLE.

Lat/Long: 53.170833, -82.531111 (Explicit)
Report Description2022/05/18 16:05 LUKE RAZAUSKAS REPORTED: DURING AN EXERCISE YESTERDAY IN THE ST. CLAIR RIVER, CCG ER STAFF LOCATED A SUBMERGED AND ABANDONED VESSEL IN POSITION 42° 35" 53.1708" 82° 31" 51.924". THE VESSEL APPEARS TO BE A 14-16FT FIBERGLASS PLEASURE BOAT WITH AN OUTBOARD MOTOR. THE MOTOR DOES NOT HAVE ITS COVER, AND THE MACHINERY IS COVERED IN ALGAE GROWTH. NO SIGNS OF POLLUTION WERE OBSERVED. IT APPEARS AS THOUGH THE VESSEL HAS BEEN SUBMERGED FOR SOME TIME - EVIDENT BY THE ALGAE GROWTH OVER IT. THE VESSEL IS LOCATED IN ABOUT 3-4FT OF WATER AT THE EDGE OF THE NORTHERN ENTRANCE TO THE CHEMATOGAN CHANNEL OF WALPOLE ISLAND FIRST NATION. THE VESSEL APPEARED STATIONARY IN ITS CURRENT POSITION, SUBMERGED AND AGROUND IN THE MUD AND GRASS, EVEN CONSIDERING THE 1-2 KNOT CURRENT. NO IDENTIFYING MARKS WERE VISIBLE, LOCAL WALPOLE ISLAND OBSERVERS PRESENT FOR THE EXERCISE WERE UNAWARE OF THE VESSEL WHEN QUESTIONED. ER STAFF WERE PRESENT AT THIS SAME LOCATION DURING AN EXERCISE IN THE SUMMER OF 2021, AND DID NOT NOTICE THIS WRECK AT THAT TIME.

CLAIR RIVER, CCG ER STAFF LOCATED A SUBMERGED AND ABANDONED VESSEL IN POSITION 42° 35" 53.1708" 82° 31" 51.924". THE VESSEL APPEARS TO BE A 14-16FT FIBERGLASS PLEASURE BOAT WITH AN OUTBOARD MOTOR. THE MOTOR DOES NOT HAVE ITS COVER, AND THE MACHINERY IS COVERED IN ALGAE GROWTH. NO SIGNS OF POLLUTION WERE OBSERVED. IT APPEARS AS THOUGH THE VESSEL HAS BEEN SUBMERGED FOR SOME TIME - EVIDENT BY THE ALGAE GROWTH OVER IT. THE VESSEL IS LOCATED IN ABOUT 3-4FT OF WATER AT THE EDGE OF THE NORTHERN ENTRANCE TO THE CHEMATOGAN CHANNEL OF WALPOLE ISLAND FIRST NATION. THE VESSEL APPEARED STATIONARY IN ITS CURRENT POSITION, SUBMERGED AND AGROUND IN THE MUD AND GRASS, EVEN CONSIDERING THE 1-2 KNOT CURRENT. NO IDENTIFYING MARKS WERE VISIBLE, LOCAL WALPOLE ISLAND OBSERVERS PRESENT FOR THE EXERCISE WERE UNAWARE OF THE VESSEL WHEN QUESTIONED. ER STAFF WERE PRESENT AT THIS SAME LOCATION DURING AN EXERCISE IN THE SUMMER OF 2021, AND DID NOT NOTICE THIS WRECK AT THAT TIME.
